# Which scripts build the app's data, and what does each do?

Every runnable script under the pipeline, listed straight off the filesystem and grouped by
what it is for. This page exists because [`etl-pipeline.md`](./etl-pipeline.md) used to keep
this list by hand and it drifted — it named a third of the scripts and missed an entire
family — so the list is now generated and that document points here for it. What is *not*
generated, and stays in `etl-pipeline.md`, is the part a filesystem cannot know: how the data
flows from the printed page to the shards, and why each step is shaped the way it is.

Nothing here is authored. Each script's one-line description is read out of the code map
([`../map.json`](../map.json)); a script the map does not yet name is marked so, which is the
honest state and a small invitation to name it. Change a script or its map note, then run
`make etl-scripts-doc`.

**69 scripts**, 59 described in the code map, 10 not yet.

## Builders — the only scripts that write the committed shards — 11

- `build-adjacency.mjs` — Dataset + curated edges → 114 shards.
- `build-alignment.mjs` — The driver and the report.
- `build-mark-adjudication.mjs` — Renders the session to one self-contained page: two panels, one rectangle each, no verdict, no feedback, no answers in the payload.
- `build-mark-nudge.mjs` — The placement page: one panel, the page's own outlines, and one rectangle that always starts 3 units off.
- `build-mark-report.mjs` — The page that asks what *kind* of wrong, and the only instrument here whose answer is not a number.
- `build-roots.mjs` — _not in the code map_
- `build-sittings-index.mjs` — The front door to the sittings, and the reason it is a script at all.
- `build-tajweed.mjs` — The eighteen-to-seven table, and the only place it exists.
- `build-words.mjs` — The builder: 604 shards of word boxes on our viewBox, plus word-boxes.pin.json (a SHA-256 per upstream page and per shard).
- `extract-pages.mjs` — Source SVG → the page asset plus its polygon manifest.
- `vendor-pages.mjs` — Loop 4b: the whole print, fetched from the pinned upstream, optimised the way Loop 0 optimised its three, and written unpadded (8.svg, not 008.svg).

## Probes — measure what a gate structurally cannot — 13

- `probe-diacritics.mjs` — The measurement that had to come before anything shipped, over all 604 cached pages: the vocabulary is complete (26 of 26 names drawn), every one of 326,515 marks lands inside the word box the app…
- `probe-encodings.mjs` — The generator: reads the 378 MB gitignored cache, the vendored tajweed offsets and the committed alignment pin, and writes one self-contained HTML file.
- `probe-hop-recall.mjs` — _not in the code map_
- `probe-ligature-print.mjs` — Asks of a corpus we have not adopted the one question adoption turns on: which print does it paginate?
- `probe-mark-counts.mjs` — The fourth mark question, and the only one that can see a mark that is NOT there.
- `probe-mark-ink.mjs` — Asks the question nothing before it asked: does a mark's rectangle sit on the ink a reader's eye goes to?
- `probe-mark-labels.mjs` — The other half of the split, and the split is the point: whether a mark's rectangle is in the right PLACE and whether its NAME is right were once one number — "51.15%, or 69.15% counting look-alike…
- `probe-mark-names.mjs` — The third question a mark can be asked, and the one the two above are blind to.
- `probe-ornament-witness.mjs` — The one measurement in this whole line of work that is not fitted to the thing it is graded by.
- `probe-piece-union.mjs` — _not in the code map_
- `probe-print-spans.mjs` — Prices the-hop-could-be-computed-from-the-print (what-we-depend-on ⑦): if the uniqueness rule ran over the print's own words instead of the morphology's, how many shipped spans survive?
- `probe-tajweed-words.mjs` — The third index nobody planned for: the tajweed annotations are CODEPOINT offsets into a Tanzil Uthmani text this repo does not hold, so neither word index reaches them.
- `probe-word-registration.mjs` — The second question about the same unadopted corpus, and the one word-level selection was blocked on: do their word boxes land on our paper?

## Scoring & settling — turn a reader's marks into a ledger — 5

- `score-mark-adjudication.mjs` — Rebuilds the key from the seed and only then learns what the answers were — which is the whole defence of the result, since nobody had to be trusted not to peek at something that did not exist.
- `score-mark-nudge.mjs` — Turns placements into a distance.
- `score-mark-report.mjs` — Reads a sitting of the five-word page, and it is built around four things it refuses to do.
- `score-piece-union-guard.mjs` — _not in the code map_
- `settle-mark-report.mjs` — Turns the sittings somebody has sat into a ruling in the repository — one row per mark, checked in beside every other ruling.

## Reports & samples — run by hand, output for a person — 3

- `audit-corpus.mjs` — Does the corpus actually cover what we claim?
- `audit-mark-sittings.mjs` — Asks whether the sittings on disk are the ones anybody should still be sitting, which until 2026-08-17 was the only step of the review routine with no command behind it — *confirm the deal did not…
- `sample-edges.mjs` — The only output of this pipeline whose consumer is a person.

## Local viewers — serve a report to a browser — 1

- `serve-sittings.mjs` — What makes an answer survive the browser losing it.

## Shared libraries — read by the scripts above, write nothing — 19

- `lib/mark-settle.mjs` — What one mark ended up saying, out of everything that was said about it — the one copy of that arithmetic, imported by both the scorer and the settler.
- `lib/mark-shape.mjs` — One library of canonical examples, shared by both probes so they cannot drift into two vocabularies.
- `lib/marks.mjs` — One page of marks, read once and cached: the ligature corpus's own <path data-diacritic> boxes put onto our frame through applierFromPin, each carrying the surah, ayah and word index of the word it…
- `lib/mushaf-frame.mjs` — The one copy of the arithmetic that puts two prints of the same page into one coordinate system.
- `lib/placement-stats.mjs` — The estimators behind a placing session, split out of the scorer for one reason: an interval is the only thing in that output nobody can eyeball for correctness, and a bracket half its true width r…
- `lib/registration-grain.mjs` — Over what group are four numbers enough?
- `lib/segmentation.mjs` — The one copy of the alignment, in two halves: the aligner (needs the upstream corpus) and the reader (needs only this repo).
- `lib/sitting-file.mjs` — One reading of a built sitting, for the same reason answered.mjs exists and with a worse failure if it did not.
- `lib/sittings-view.mjs` — The front door's arithmetic and its wording, written once and run twice — in Node to bake a page that is true when it is written and readable with nothing serving it, and in the browser against wha…
- `lib/tailnet.mjs` — The one address a sitting is reached at, and the reason there has to be exactly one.
- `lib/tajweed-fold.mjs` — The ONE copy of the fold arithmetic — the reconstruction of the Tanzil-indexed string out of the print's per-word data-hafs, under the eight corrections CORRECTIONS names, dates and prices in evide…
